approach: The fault starts in the Claude driver, which reports a deadline kill as the generic `Killed`, and in the producer loop (`run.rs`), which treats any non-Success producer as `failed` before the change list is read, so the snapshot's edits are never turned into a candidate. Fix: (1) add a distinct `TimedOut` invocation outcome, set only on the deadline path, and a `TimedOut` job outcome state (additive serde variants, so old records still load). (2) When the producer ends `TimedOut`, build the candidate commit from the snapshot's change list (the same step the success path runs), write a progress note to the job's records, keep the work directory, and close the job `timed_out` with the deadline text as the reason. (3) Let "try again on <job>" accept a timed-out job: the tree-retry seed starts from the kept candidate commit and the producer brief carries the progress note. (4) Status/closing output shows `timed_out`, which differs from `failed`. Producer stage only. The note text comes from one function that reads data already recorded (deadline detail, changed paths, commands run), so the file and the retry brief cannot differ.

decisions.choice: New `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut` and `OutcomeState::TimedOut` variants, not a flag on `Killed`/`Failed`.
decisions.reason: The driver currently folds deadline and kill switch into `Killed`; a kill-switch stop must not be resumable. Additive snake_case variants leave every existing record deserializing unchanged.

rejected.option: Keep `Killed` and detect the deadline by parsing the detail string 'deadline of Ns reached'
rejected.why: Prose matching is fragile and would make status depend on wording.

rejected.option: Record the job as `failed` with a note
rejected.why: The request asks for timed out, distinct from failed; status could not tell them apart from state.

decisions.choice: Keep the work by committing a candidate commit (loose object, on no branch) from the snapshot change list, reusing the existing tree-seed path (`SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree`) for the retry.
decisions.reason: Retry already seeds a work tree from a candidate commit; the commit survives in the user's repo and the records reference it, so resume works even if the job's work directory is later cleaned. Fixes the root cause where edits are dropped.

rejected.option: Reuse the old work directory in place for the retry
rejected.why: The retry job has a new id and job dir, and run.rs deletes `work` at producer start; a path dependency on another job's dir is brittle.
Bloats the records branch when a commit object already holds them.

decisions.choice: The progress note is generated by one function from recorded data (deadline detail, changed paths, commands run), written as `progress-note.md` beside the job's records and embedded in the retry brief.
decisions.reason: No second source of truth; the retry reads only records, as the other retry seeds do.

rejected.option: Ask the timed-out agent to write a note
rejected.why: It is killed at the deadline and cannot be relied on.

rejected.option: Write the note into the work tree
rejected.why: It would end up in the retry's candidate diff.

decisions.choice: Skip admission and verification for a timed-out candidate; it is only kept, never landed.
decisions.reason: Partial work should not be judged; the retry's full candidate is verified normally.

rejected.why: Wastes verifier budget on unfinished work and goes beyond the request.

files.purpose: Add `OutcomeState::TimedOut` (as_str 'timed_out') and `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut`; fix the Killed doc; add the legacy-deserialize test.
Add a small `KillReason { Deadline, KillSwitch }` enum for the driver to use, with a test.
Report a deadline kill as `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut` and a kill-switch kill as `Killed`; update its tests at lines ~684 and ~715.
Treat `TimedOut` like `Killed` for `completed` (no measured usage or cost); edits are already applied before the outcome.
Update the module doc and cost handling so a timed-out invocation is recorded with lower-bound tokens and a cap-bounded cost like a killed one.

In the producer loop, on `TimedOut`, build the candidate commit from the change list, put the progress note in the closing files, set `Happened.state` to `TimedOut` with the deadline reason, keep the work dir; build `RetrySeed` with the note; treat TimedOut with Failed in `go` follow-ups where needed.
`earlier_attempt_with` accepts `Closed(TimedOut)`; `tree_retry_seed` returns a seed for a timed-out job with a progress note built by a shared `progress_note` function; tests.
`RetrySeed` gets `progress_note: Option<String>`; `retry_section` renders a resume section for it; update the existing test fixture.
Add a 'next' line for `timed_out` (retry with 'try again on <job>').
Mark a timed-out job retryable alongside Rejected and Failed (line ~708).
Test for the producer deadline: state, kept edit, note, reason.
Test that drain treats a timed-out job as retryable and not failed.
Test that a retry of a timed-out job starts from the kept tree and sees the note (not in the expected list; it holds `run_retry`).
Document the `timed_out` outcome state and invocation outcome.
Unreleased entry for keep-and-resume on a producer deadline.

steps: records.rs: add the two TimedOut variants and as_str; add the test that legacy 'killed' and 'failed' JSON still parse. Build, then fix the non-exhaustive matches the compiler reports.

procs.rs: add `KillReason`. claude.rs: in the wait loop record the reason; return `TimedOut` with detail 'deadline of Ns reached' for the deadline and `Killed` for the kill switch; adjust the two claude.rs tests.
fake.rs: `completed` is false for Killed and TimedOut. invocation.rs: doc line and any outcome-dependent handling.

reading.rs: a `progress_note(reason, changes, commands)` function; extend `earlier_attempt_with` to allow `Closed(TimedOut)` and `tree_retry_seed` to seed a timed-out job that has a candidate commit; add `progress_note` to `TreeRetrySeed`.
briefs.rs: add the field and the resume section; update the fixture.

run.rs: in the producer loop, before the non-Success failure return, handle `TimedOut`: read `snapshot.change_list()`, make the candidate commit as the success path does (reuse by extracting a small helper), push `progress-note.md`, set the state and reason, and return the closing. If there are no changes, close `timed_out` with no candidate and the note says nothing was kept. Pass the progress note into `RetrySeed` in `dispatch`.
display.rs and drain.rs: the timed_out next-step line and retry flag.
Add tests: lifecycle.rs, retry.rs, drain.rs, using a scripted fake producer that edits and returns TimedOut.
Run cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Non-exhaustive matches on `OutcomeState`/`InvocationOutcome` elsewhere (steward.rs, introspect.rs, gate, score) break the build or misclassify the new state.
risks.mitigation: Let the compiler list them; treat TimedOut like Failed for cost and scoring unless there is a reason not to; review each hit.

risks.risk: The candidate commit is a loose object that git gc could prune before the retry.
risks.mitigation: `tree_seed` already checks `rev_parse` and falls back to a base start; the progress note still reaches the retry brief. Noted as a limit.

risks.risk: The retry's `tree_seed` refuses to seed when the base changed beyond records/, so a retry after other work lands starts clean.
risks.mitigation: Keep the existing guard to avoid undoing later work; the note is still given to the retry producer.

risks.risk: Old Athena builds reading the new `timed_out` state fail to parse.
risks.mitigation: Additive only; a changelog line says records written with `timed_out` need this version.

demonstrations.method: Integration test in lifecycle.rs: a scripted fake producer writes a file and returns outcome TimedOut with detail 'deadline of 1800s reached'. Run the job.
demonstrations.observes: The finished job's state is `OutcomeState::TimedOut` (not Failed). The job's candidate record has a commit that contains the edited file. `progress-note.md` exists in the job's records and names the edited path. The work directory still holds the edit.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the driver and run.rs unchanged the fake's TimedOut turn would close the job `failed`, create no candidate, and write no note, so the assertions on state timed_out, the kept edit and the note file would fail.

demonstrations.method: Test in retry.rs (uses its `run_retry` helper): time out a job after an edit, then retry it with a second scripted producer that records what it saw.
demonstrations.observes: At the retry producer's start the kept file exists in its working directory (not a clean base). The producer's prompt contains the progress note text and the deadline reason. The retry is accepted for a timed-out job.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the retry change, 'try again on <job>' would be refused for a timed-out job, or would start from a clean base checkout with no note, so the test's checks for the kept file and the note in the brief would fail.

demonstrations.method: Same lifecycle test, plus a drain.rs test, checking the user-facing output and the stored outcome record.
demonstrations.observes: The finished text reads `outcome timed_out · …deadline of 1800s reached…`, not `failed`. The stored outcome record has state timed_out and the reason holding the deadline text. The drain test shows a timed-out job is flagged retryable.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the outcome stayed `failed` or lost its reason, the status/finish output would read 'failed' and the deadline text would be missing.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in records.rs: deserialize an invocation with outcome `killed` and an outcome record with state `failed` from the existing JSON shapes, and round-trip them.
demonstrations.observes: Both parse and re-serialize byte-identical; `timed_out` parses to the new variants.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the new variants changed existing names or serde tags, the legacy JSON fixtures would not parse.

demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased has an entry on timed-out producers that keep work and resume. docs/records.md lists `timed_out` among the outcome states and `timed_out` for the invocation outcome.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0 with no warnings.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any non-exhaustive match on the new variants, or a warning, would fail the build or `-D warnings`.

open_questions: Whether the job's `work` directory is deleted when a job closes; the code read did not show it. The plan keeps the candidate commit as the durable copy either way.
Whether a timed-out job should be introspected like Rejected and Failed (`go` does so at run.rs:145); the plan leaves it out to keep the change small.
The exact `athena retry` command surface: the code read shows retry as a request of the form 'try again on <job>' (reading.rs RETRY_PREFIX), which the plan extends.
Which `OutcomeState` matches elsewhere need a TimedOut arm; the compiler will list them.
